At UTC, research reaches from the lab to the launchpad.
 Dr. Reetesh Ranjan, an associate professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, develops and applies multi-scale models of turbulence, a longstanding challenge in fluid dynamics with applications in combustion and energy conversion, rocket propulsion, high-speed aerodynamics and stratified ocean flows.
 Over the years, his research has received support from several federal agencies, including the National Science Foundation, the Office of Naval Research and the Air Force Office of Scientific Research. He has collaborated with researchers across leading institutions, including the Georgia Institute of Technology, the University of Central Florida, the University of Alabama in Huntsville, the University of Cincinnati and the Air Force Research Laboratory.
 🔗  Read more here: https://blog.utc.edu/…/behind-the-research-at-utc-dr-reete…/

items.content_text:
OECD projections show that New Zealand’s GDP growth is expected to gradually strengthen, reaching 1.4% in 2026 and 2.3% in 2027. However, recent rises in energy prices are likely to slow the pace of growth.
 Higher fuel costs are pushing up inflation in the short term, while increased uncertainty around the global economy and fuel supply is expected to weigh on consumer and business confidence. This could delay spending and investment decisions.
 Overall, while the outlook points to gradually improving growth, careful economic policy management will be needed to keep growth on track.
 Read the #OECD Economic Survey of New Zealand: https://brnw.ch/21x4ptS
 #BetterPoliciesForBetterLives

Meet the Amazing Team Behind Summer Camp at Avondale Community Center! 
 Our summer camp counselors are so much more than activity leaders—they're mentors, role models, and positive influences who help create unforgettable experiences for our campers each day. Their dedication, compassion, and leadership make a lasting impact on the children and families we serve, and we're proud to recognize them!

 👏 Ronta Taylor – Sophomore at Middle Tennessee State University, majoring in Electrical and Mechanical Engineering. A former Avondale participant, Ronta loves giving back to the community that helped shape him. "I Am Avondale!"

 Thank you to these outstanding young leaders for investing their time, talents, and hearts into our campers this summer. Your commitment is helping shape the next generation, and we couldn't be more grateful!

 From: Jon Holmes, City Manager
 Date: 07/24/2026

 City Administration:
 * Discussion with Chattanooga Gas regarding a Pressure Regulator Station infrastructure upgrade reques
 * Finalize Freedom Fest After Action Notes

 * ﻿﻿We are working to obtain quotes for an 8ft agricultural mesh wire style fence, to secure the airport perimeter from wildlife. Quotes will include installation and surveyor costs to define the property line on the west side of the airport.
 * ﻿﻿Our Airport Capital Improvement Plan (ACIP) working session is scheduled for the 7th of August as well. While our engineer and TDOT project manager are present on-site, we will be reviewing possible solutions to rehabilitate the McDonald Terrace taxiway easement on the north end of the Airport.
 * ﻿﻿The challenge that we have been facing with that project remains to be equipment mobilization, due to the thickness of our pavement, resulting in a lower weight bearing capacity that standard equipment will exceed. The Public Works Director will be a part of that meeting as well, for additional engineering and project management expertise.
 * ﻿﻿We rolled out the advertisement for letters of interest with the Airport Advisory Board that was approved at the last regular session Commission meeting. The application period is open until August 21st.

Hamilton County’s Alternative Sentencing Programs team is making a real difference across our community—helping keep our roads, waterways, and neighborhoods clean.
 Community service crews cleaned nearly 58 miles of local roads and highways, collecting 327 bags of litter. They also partnered with Keep Tennessee Rivers Beautiful to collect and recycle more than 60 tires removed from along the river and addressed illegal dumping sites on Lake Resort Drive.
 Thank you to the dedicated officers, supervisors, and participants whose work strengthens our community every day. Residents can also properly dispose of tires at the recycling center next to Silverdale for just $1 per tire.

Until then, keep making waves 💙

🏆 The Southeast Tennessee Development District was the only organization in Tennessee to receive a 2026 Excellence in Regional Transportation Award from the National Association of Development Organizations (NADO) — and we're incredibly proud to celebrate this achievement.

This week, Rohan Thompson (pictured center in this photo), Regional Planner and Southeast RPO Coordinator, accepted the award on behalf of SETD's Regional Planning Organization (RPO) program during the 2026 National Regional Transportation Conference in Atlanta.

The award recognizes the Dunlap Bicycle and Pedestrian Plan, a collaborative effort that is helping create a safer, more connected future for the City of Dunlap while supporting long-term transportation planning, economic development, and quality of life.

This recognition reflects the dedication of our RPO and Planning team and the strong partnerships among the City of Dunlap, the Tennessee Department of Transportation, local stakeholders, and community members who helped bring this vision to life.

Congratulations to Rohan, RPO, and our Planning team on this outstanding national achievement. We are honored to represent Southeast Tennessee on the national stage!

HCSO Involved in Vehicle Pursuit, Suspect Arrested After Fleeing and Hiding in Hotel Along with 2 Fugitives with Several Active Warrants
 Hamilton County, TN - Yesterday, on July 22, 2026, an HCSO Traffic Investigator attempted to conduct a traffic stop on a vehicle whose driver was exhibiting behavior indicative of a DUI while traveling south on Highway 153. The vehicle then fled, and a pursuit was initiated. Due to the reckless driving of the suspect and heavy traffic conditions around the I-75 / I-24 split, the HCSO Traffic Unit made the decision to terminate pursuit of the vehicle.
 A short time later, Tennessee Highway Patrol Trooper Caldwell found the suspect’s abandoned vehicle parked at McKay’s Bookstore.
 Through investigative processes, HSCO deputies focused their search on a room at America's Best Inn, located across the street from the abandoned vehicle. The suspect was found hiding under a bed in the room, along with 2 other wanted fugitives with active warrants, who were not involved in the pursuit. The vehicle key was also found in the room.
 This investigation was a success thanks to the coordination between HCSO Patrol, Traffic, K9, Criminal Warrants, and Crime Analysis Units. We would also like to extend special thanks for the collaboration and support of our partners with the Tennessee Highway Patrol, whose efforts were instrumental in these arrests.
 The following individuals were arrested and transported to the Hamilton County Jail and Detention Center; their warrants and charges are as follows:
 Nikkarra Crisp:
 (2) Active Sessions Court Warrants for: 
 • Aggravated Burglary 
 • Theft of Property
 Additional Charges:
 • Felony Evading Arrest 
 • DUI (Second Offense) 
 • Evading Arrest
 • Reckless Driving
 • Failure to Exercise Due Care
 • Speeding
 • Failure to Wear a Seat Belt
 Brando Moates:
 (6) Active Sessions Court Warrants for:
 • Theft of Property (x2)
 • Possession of a Firearm During the Commission of a Felony
 • Possession of a Firearm with Intent to Go Armed
 • Aggravated Burglary
 • Theft of Property
 (4) Active Criminal Court Warrants for: 
 • Possession of Methamphetamine for Resale
 • Possession of Fentanyl with Intent to Manufacture
 • Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Violent Felon
 • Possession of Drug Paraphernalia
 Bahja Fox:
 Active Sessions Court Warrant for: 
 • Aggravated Burglary
 Additional Active Warrants from the City of East Ridge for:
 • Forgery and Theft Over $2,500
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

Young people are cast as the face of climate action, so why are they among the most underrepresented voices in London's green transition?  
 
We're taking that question to City Hall.   
 
🌱 Re-thinking green transitions with young Londoners  
🗓 Wednesday 23 September 2026, 10am–2pm  
📍 City Hall, London  
 
Over the past year, a team of peer researchers from across the capital has been exploring why young Londoners are so often left out of decisions on climate, nature, green jobs and infrastructure, and what it would take to change that.   
 
This half-day conference shares their findings and turns them into action, convening local authority participation leads and officers, youth climate activists, councillors, funders, civil society and academics.  
 
In partnership with Partnership for Young London and Islington Council.  
 
Register your interest now: https://lnkd.in/eTZfsUFk 
 
#GreenTransition #YouthClimateAction #London

Young people are cast as the face of climate action, so why are they among the most underrepresented voices in London's green transition? 

We're taking that question to City Hall.  

🌱 Re-thinking green transitions with young Londoners 
🗓 Wednesday 23 September 2026, 10am–2pm 
📍 City Hall, London 

Over the past year, a team of peer researchers from across the capital has been exploring why young Londoners are so often left out of decisions on climate, nature, green jobs and infrastructure, and what it would take to change that.  

This half-day conference shares their findings and turns them into action, convening local authority participation leads and officers, youth climate activists, councillors, funders, civil society and academics. 

In partnership with Partnership for Young London and Islington Council. 

Register your interest now:  https://lnkd.in/eTZfsUFk

For the past three weeks, Southeast Conservation Corps Youth Crew 957 has been laying the groundwork for a brand-new trail at the up-and-coming Provence Street Park.
 When this project began, the area was heavily overrun with invasive plants. Thanks to our partnership with Wild Violet Permaculture, the site was prepped and cleared, allowing the crew to jump in and do the heavy lifting of constructing the actual path.
 We’re so proud of these crew members for their dedication and hard work over the last several weeks, and deeply grateful for our partnership with SECC for helping make this project possible.
 (Look closely at the bottom of the first photo. Can you spot the SECC crew hard at work? It really puts the scale of this project into perspective! 🔍)

items.content_text:
HCSO Involved in Vehicle Pursuit Yesterday with Successful PIT Maneuver, Suspect Arrested in Georgia
 Hamilton County, TN - Yesterday, on July 21, 2026, detectives from the HCSO Criminal Warrants Unit located a suspect with active felony warrants out of Walker County, Georgia. As they attempted to take the subject into custody, he entered his vehicle and fled. Deputies pursued the vehicle down Rossville Boulevard to I-24.
 The suspect continued west on I-24, driving erratically, and eventually crossed the TN-GA border. Once the vehicle slowed, an HCSO deputy was able to safely conduct a PIT maneuver on the suspect’s vehicle.
 Due to the pursuit ending in Georgia, the suspect, identified as Kennie Montieth, was transferred into the custody of Georgia authorities. Montieth was charged with the outstanding felony warrants in Georgia, and additional charges were obtained in both Tennessee and Georgia.
 Charges in Dade County, GA
 • Aggravated Assault Police Officer
 • Improper Lane Change/Failure to Maintain Lane
 • No Insurance
 • Willful Obstruction of Law Enforcement Officers by Use of Threats or Violence- Felony
 • Willful Obstruction of Law Enforcement Officers-Misdemeanor
 New Charges in Hamilton County:
 • Evading Arrest
 • Reckless Endangerment
 • Aggravated Assault
 • Driving an Unregistered Vehicle
 • Driving Without a License
 • Speeding
 • Failure to Maintain Lane
 • Reckless Driving 
 Due to the suspect being taken into custody in Georgia we will not be providing the mugshot of Mr. Montieth, please reach out to the Dade County Sheriff’s Office for further information. 
 This information is preliminary and subject to change. No further details are available.

Did you know that over 1,000 children have died from heatstroke in vehicles since 1998? 
 More than half of these tragedies occurred when a child was unintentionally forgotten in the back seat. These deaths can be prevented! 
 If you see a child alone in a vehicle, check on them immediately. If they are unresponsive or seem to be in distress, call 911 right away. 
 For more information, visit https://www.nhtsa.gov/campaign/heatstroke

 Once the survey closes, Sensemaking AI technology will identify common priorities among residents. items.title: On Friday, July 17, the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP) released a proposed rewrite of the federal regu...
items.content_text:
On Friday, July 17, the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP) released a proposed rewrite of the federal regulations implementing Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, one of the nation's most important tools for protecting historic places.
 If adopted, these changes would dramatically reduce public participation and shift much of the decision-making authority to federal agencies. Among the proposed changes are:
 • Limiting opportunities for meaningful consultation with State Historic Preservation Offices, Tribal Nations, local governments, and preservation organizations.
 • Narrowing when historic resources are reviewed and what qualifies for protection.
 • Weakening requirements to avoid, minimize, or mitigate impacts to historic places.
 For more than 60 years, Section 106 has helped balance infrastructure, economic development, and community growth with the preservation of our nation's historic and cultural resources. It has never been about stopping projects. It has been about making better decisions through collaboration.
 Learn more at: https://culturalheritagepartners.com/war-room-for-threats-…/
 These proposed changes could affect how historic places across Tennessee, including those here in Chattanooga, are identified, reviewed, and protected. Stay informed, share this post, and follow Preserve Chattanooga as we continue advocating for preservation policies that give our community a voice in shaping its future.
